document.abstract: This paper describes a project of the University of Greenwich, London, employing metadata to increase the usefulness of objects produced by the broadcasting and film industries in more general industrial contexts. Within the construction industry, planning for large-scale projects requires integration of conventionally shot and edited video, computer-generated video, and VR models. These are merged with various CAD and related models to produce a complex object capable of being viewed by those wishing to extract information with views relevant to their speciality. Managing this complexity is difficult and the paper presents XML-based metadata and object-oriented database technology as a practical technical basis upon which to build such a project integration tool.

authors.bio: After graduating from the University of Essex with a Ph.D. in computer science, Christopher Woollard worked for Wang Laboratories as a principal engineer on distributed computer architectures; this work culminated in the Wang Distributed Database Machine. In the late 1980s he was principal operating systems engineer at Thinking Machines Corp. working on the CM-2 supercomputer. He then took up his current position with the University of Greenwich, London. Concurrently, Woollard has been a working cinematographer undertaking various second unit feature and television projects in the U.S. and U.K. He has presented papers on various Greenwich-based film and television oriented research projects at previous SMPTE Conferences.
